Her element, carried in her design: darmstadtium: a heavy synthetic metal below platinum, first made in 1994 by striking lead with nickel ions fired down a long straight accelerator in a research city that found six new elements, and named for that city, where an art-nouveau artists' colony was built on a hill in 1899 around a tall brick tower crowned with five rounded fingers and walls of golden mosaic, and where electrical engineering was first taught as a university subject.

Colours: art-nouveau gold mosaic, deep plum, ion-beam turquoise, warm brick red.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE

Stance and hands: Her open hands rest at her sides, with separation from her sleeves and body.

Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.

Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.
